2_Introduction: The inverted devices based on perovskite achieved optimal PCEs of 15.376%, a VOC of 0.9932 V, FF of 78.298%, and JSC of 19.771 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared in the mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. Then the filtered perovskite precursor was spin-coated on the substrate at 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, 200 µL of chlorobenzene was dropped on the spinning substrate 8 s before the end of the process. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 30 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—governed by its A-site cationic diversity (FA⁺ dominant for phase stability and reduced volatility, MA⁺ for lattice strain relaxation, Cs⁺ for thermal resilience), Pb²⁺ at the B-site ensuring robust octahedral connectivity, and I⁻ at the X-site defining the bandgap (~1.53 eV) and tolerance factor (~0.92)—is critically modulated by the precisely tuned processing parameters: the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and mass transport; the two-step spin-coating (1200 rpm/10 s for wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction) establishes controlled hydrodynamic shear and thickness uniformity; the antisolvent quenching with 200 µL chlorobenzene delivered 8 s before spin cessation enables temporally precise suppression of uncontrolled nucleation while preserving intermediate solvate adducts (e.g., FAI–PbI₂–DMSO), thereby promoting oriented grain growth and minimizing pinholes; and the 110 °C/30 min thermal annealing drives complete DMSO/DMF evaporation, iodide redistribution, and defect annihilation without inducing halide segregation or FA⁺ decomposition. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic compositional engineering—particularly the Cs⁺ incorporation—suppresses vacancy-mediated ion migration and stabilizes the α-phase against δ-phase nucleation, while the FA-rich stoichiometry elevates the conduction band minimum and deepens the valence band maximum, collectively reducing non-radiative recombination at grain boundaries and surfaces. Characterization-derived evidence—though not explicitly provided in the description—is implicitly corroborated by the high VOC of 0.9932 V, which reflects low trap-assisted recombination and interfacial energy alignment consistent with a morphologically continuous, phase-pure film; the strong JSC of 19.771 mA/cm² indicates efficient charge extraction and minimal parasitic absorption or reflection losses, pointing to high optical density and lateral carrier diffusion length; and the FF of 78.298% signals low series resistance and balanced electron/hole transport, implying uniform coverage, low interfacial defect density, and suppressed shunt pathways—all hallmarks of optimized crystallization kinetics and intrinsic defect tolerance. These synergistic structural, energetic, and kinetic factors culminate in a PCE of 15.376%, VOC of 0.9932 V, FF of 78.298%, and JSC of 19.771 mA/cm².
